organizations.name: International Agency for Research on Cancer
organizations.note: WHO's cancer agency in Lyon, established by World Health Assembly resolution WHA18.44 (1965) but governed by its own Statute and its own 30 Participating States; the Governing Council, not the Health Assembly, adopts its budget and programme.

documents.note: Every Governing and Scientific Council session links to an Indico event holding the full document set, including adopted resolutions (a consolidated resolutions PDF for 2025; 22 individually numbered resolution PDFs for 2026), in English and French. Free from March 2009 onward; earlier sessions need registration. A per-session archive, not a resolutions database — borderline

mandates.note: Nothing distinguishes in-force from superseded or completed resolutions; the archive is chronological

budget.note: The Governing Council adopts the biennial Programme and Budget as one document by resolution, but no budget information is attached to individual mandates

implementation.note: The standing 'Director's response' series answers Scientific Council recommendations, not Governing Council resolutions; no per-resolution follow-up found

results.note: Scientific output is reported through the Biennial Report and Medium-Term Strategy evaluation, by branch and strategic objective, not against named resolutions

organizations.name: Pan American Health Organization
organizations.note: A separate inter-American treaty organization founded in 1902, with its own constitution, 35 Member States and three-tier governance, that simultaneously serves as WHO's Regional Office for the Americas — each Directing Council session is also a session of the WHO Regional Committee.

documents.note: Faceted listing (200+ topic terms, date range) of PAHO resolutions, plans of action and strategies; per-session document pages for every body; full texts in IRIS, a DSpace 7 repository with a public REST API

mandates.note: CD62/INF/3 (5 Aug 2025) classifies resolutions as Active / Conditional Active / Sunset against criteria printed in the document, on a cycle mandated by resolution CD55.R11 (2016), editions 2016/2019/2022/2025. Coverage is partial: the report carries the 131 resolutions still carried forward out of 403 adopted 1999-2024, and the 272 already sunset are excluded. Supersession is named per resolution in the internal annex, but the publicly linked 'Active PAHO Resolutions' extract omits the Sunset rows and the supersession statements.

budget.note: Program Budget and pbdigital.paho.org are organized by Strategic Plan outcome/output, country and biennium; no monetary amounts attached to individual resolutions

implementation.note: The monitoring report assesses per resolution whether the commitments in the operative paragraphs have been met or remain in force, and whether the stipulated progress reports were presented, publishing Reporting Requirement / Report(s) / Status / Justification per resolution — a triennial PDF table, not a tracker

results.note: Per-resolution final and progress report series to the Governing Bodies on resolution-endorsed plans of action (e.g. CD62/INF/5, CD62/INF/6, CD62/INF/8), indexed by the monitoring annex; same weak form as WHO's consolidated WHA progress reports

organizations.name: Unitaid
organizations.note: A hosted partnership of WHO: WHO provides the administrative host and holds one of the thirteen Board seats, but Unitaid has its own Constitution, Executive Board and budget, and WHO's governing bodies have no role in its governance.

documents.note: Per-meeting listing filterable by meeting number and date, with each meeting's resolutions R1…Rn as individual PDFs plus minutes and agenda; a separate e-Resolutions tab (32 pages) with year filter and free-text keyword search; plus Constitution, Board Operating Procedures and Code of Ethical Conduct

mandates.note: No in-force, superseded or lapsed status; both tabs are chronological, and resolutions that plainly replace earlier ones are not marked

budget.note: each investment resolution authorizes an amount (e.g. R4-2026-e, up to US$18,500,000), but the decision is itself the spending authorization rather than a mandate linked to financial information: nothing aggregates the authorizations or reports disbursement against them. Same treatment as IFAD and IAEA, whose budgets are likewise adopted by their own resolutions.

implementation.note: Follow-up runs through Key Performance Indicator reports and the Executive Director's report, organized by strategic objective, not by resolution
